points.what: EMEA was the largest contributor to this week's order growth, adding 35 orders, 37.6% of the total change, on 27.1% WoW growth.
points.so_what: Growth came more from EMEA than from APAC, the largest region by share at 42.6% but a smaller contributor to the change.

points.what: Search was the top contributor to order growth, adding 42 orders, 45.2% of the total change, while growing 8.3% WoW.
points.so_what: Facebook grew 53.5% WoW but added only 23 orders to the total change, showing the order gain is concentrated in the largest channel, not spread across faster-growing smaller ones.

points.what: LATAM orders grew 32.1% WoW, contributing 26 orders, 28.0% of the total change.
points.so_what: That is a meaningful share of this week's growth coming from LATAM, the smallest region by share at 13.6%.

points.what: AOV was $83.51, down 0.2% WoW though up 0.5% YoY.
points.so_what: With AOV roughly flat, this week's revenue increase came from more orders rather than bigger baskets.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Feb 2 was 10.8%, down 0.8 pp WoW but up 2.9 pp YoY.
points.so_what: The year-on-year rise is the worse signal, so the underlying return trend has not clearly improved despite the weekly dip.

points.what: New signups rose 28.7% WoW, a notable increase, but were up only 5.1% YoY versus orders' 58.1% YoY growth.
points.so_what: New customer growth is running far behind order growth on a year-on-year basis, an imbalance to note when reading the order gains.

summary.headline: Week behind target on both orders (98.4%) and revenue (89.6%), with cancellation rate up 4.2 pp WoW and the year still behind at 87.7% YTD attainment.

points.what: Orders rose 13.4% WoW and 58.1% YoY, but reached only 98.4% of the weekly target.
points.so_what: Growth on both comparisons still was not enough to hit target, leaving orders behind for the week.

points.what: Revenue rose 7.5% WoW to $53,365, which is 89.6% of the weekly target.
points.so_what: Revenue's target attainment trails orders', pointing to weaker basket value rather than fewer orders as the shortfall.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 4.2 pp WoW to 19.0%, a notable increase that is also up 5.4 pp YoY.
points.so_what: A bad move on both comparisons is a risk to the revenue booked this week.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue attainment are both 87.7%, $58,431 behind target with 5 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter and year remain behind, requiring a faster pace than recently seen to close the gap.

points.what: Orders reached 98.4% of the weekly target and revenue reached 89.6% of its target, both behind.
points.so_what: Revenue's gap is larger than orders', keeping the week on the negative side of target overall.

points.what: QTD and YTD revenue attainment are both 87.7%, a $58,431 gap versus target with 5 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Closing the remaining $359,246 needed for the full-quarter target requires a faster pace than the recent run rate.

points.what: The required weekly revenue run rate to hit the full-year target is $77,189, versus a current 8-week run rate of $51,914.
points.so_what: At the recent pace, the full-year target is out of reach unless the run rate rises well above recent levels.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 4.2 pp WoW to 19.0%, a notable increase.
points.so_what: With each point of cancellation worth $659 in revenue, a jump this size is a meaningful revenue risk.

points.what: The current 8-week revenue run rate is $51,914, below the $77,189 required weekly run rate for the rest of the year.
points.so_what: At this pace, the full-year revenue target is out of reach.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of Feb 2 rose 2.9 pp YoY to 10.8%, even though it fell 0.8 pp WoW.
points.so_what: The year-on-year direction remains worse, a risk to watch regardless of the recent weekly dip.
